extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs, connecting language and vision to facilitate cognitive visual tasks and scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna, Yuke Zhu, Oliver Groth, Justin Johnson, Kenji Hata, Joshua Kravitz, Stephanie Chen, Yannis Kalantidis, Li-Jia Li, David A. Shamma, Michael S. Bemstein, Li Fei-Fei
extraction.citeAs: Krishna, R., Zhu, Y., Groth, O., Johnson, J., Hata, K., Kravitz, J., Chen, S., Kalantidis, Y., Li, L.-J., Shamma, D. A., Bemstein, M. S., & Fei-Fei, L. (2016). Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations. arXiv preprint arXiv:1602.07332v1.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from the intersection of MS-COCO and YFCC100M. The images are real-world, non-iconic photos uploaded onto Flickr by users, ranging from 72 to 1280 pixels in width.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 108,249 images from the intersection of MS-COCO's 328,000 images and YFCC100M's 100 million images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Collected over the course of 6 months after 15 months of experimentation and iteration on the data representation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text preprocessing included lowercasing, lemmatizing, stripping excess whitespace, removing non-alphanumeric characters, and using Stanford NLP tools for noun phrase extraction and POS normalization. Objects, attributes, and relationships were canonicalized to WordNet synsets with hand-crafted disambiguation rules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdsourced on Amazon Mechanical Turk over approximately 800,000 HITs. Tasks included writing region descriptions enforced for diversity via BLEU score thresholds (<=0.7), drawing bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality criteria, extracting objects with suggestions from Stanford dependency parser, assigning attributes and relationships to construct region graphs, merging overlapping bounding boxes (>=0.8 IoU) to form scene graphs, and generating freeform and region-based 6W question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All annotations except objects were verified using majority voting, where three unique workers evaluated each annotation and acceptance required agreement by at least two workers. Objects were verified using rapid visual judgments. Canonicalization mappings were verified and adjusted by crowd workers choosing from top alternative synsets.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Per image averages: 42 to 50 region descriptions, 21 objects, 18 attributes, 18 relationships, 1 scene graph, and 17 question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique workers; 93.02% from United States, 1.29% Philippines, 1.13% Kenya, 0.94% India, 0.50% Russia, 0.47% Canada, 2.65% Others. Gender: 54.15% male, 45.85% female. Age: majority between 25-34 years old, youngest 18, oldest 68.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford CoreNLP dependency parser, WordNet, word2vec
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Workers earned between $6-$8 per hour for continuous work, aligning with ethical research standards on Amazon Mechanical Turk. HITs achieved a 94.1% retention rate.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards images of people and sports activities (e.g., ski, ballplayer, racket). State-of-motion verbs and specific sports (skiing, surfing) are overrepresented in person attributes due to image source bias. Zipfian distribution in relationship predicates, predominantly 'on'.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Relationships exhibit high intra-class appearance variability, leading to lower classification accuracy. Baseline performance on reasoning-intensive question types (such as 'why' questions) is very low. WordNet does not support prepositions, which had to be ignored in relationship canonicalization.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking models for dense image captioning, visual question answering, cognitive scene understanding, relationship extraction, attribute prediction, and semantic image retrieval.
